issues.description: Class constructor signature mismatch for GroverLightsOutPuzzle: the template implementation (template_repository/ex4_grover_lights_out_puzzle.py) declares __init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) while the solution implementation (solution_repository/ex4_grover_lights_out_puzzle.py) declares __init__(self) with no parameter. The rest of the template code (the run() method and the grover_circuit/state_preparation methods) expects the board state to be supplied later as an argument (state_of_lights passed to grover_circuit), and example usage in the repository and problem materials instantiate or document using GroverLightsOutPuzzle() without passing an initial_state. This inconsistency will cause a runtime error or confusion when students follow the provided examples (they will be required to pass an unexpected constructor argument) and prevents a seamless mapping between the template, solution, and example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor API consistent across template, solution, and examples. Recommended fix: remove the initial_state parameter from the template constructor so the signature becomes def __init__(self): and initialize registers there (matching the solution). This preserves the intended pattern where the board state is passed later to grover_circuit/state_preparation (state_of_lights). Alternatively (less preferred), update the solution, run examples, and problem text to require and document an initial_state parameter at construction. Update any tests or example code to match the chosen signature.
